TS.short: Under EO 13526, TOP SECRET must be applied to information, the unauthorized disclosure of which reasonably could be expected to cause *exceptionally grave damage* to the national security that the original classification authority (OCA) is able to identify or describe.

S.short: Under EO 13526, SECRET must be applied to information, the unauthorized disclosure of which reasonably could be expected to cause *serious* damage to the national security that the original classification authority is able to identify or describe.

C.short: Under EO 13526, CONFIDENTIAL must be applied to information, the unauthorized disclosure of which reasonably could be expected to cause damage to the national security that the original classification authority is able to identify or describe.

U.short: A designation used to mark information that does not meet the criteria for classified (CONFIDENTIAL, SECRET or TOP SECRET) national security information as defined by EO 13526.

SI.short: Special Intelligence, or SI, is an SCI control system designed to protect technical and intelligence information derived from monitoring foreign communications signals by other than the intended recipients.
SI.long: Special Intelligence, or SI, is an SCI control system designed to protect technical and intelligence information derived from monitoring foreign communications signals by other than the intended recipients. The SI control system protects SI-derived information and information relating to SI activities, capabilities, techniques, process and procedures.
SI.plain: Special Intelligence (SI) is one of the main SCI control systems. It protects intelligence drawn from intercepting foreign communications and other signals, along with the sources and methods behind it.
tips: SI is a control system — a portion names it after the classification: TOP SECRET//SI.
SI compartments such as GAMMA (written SI-G) restrict a piece of SI further; access to SI does not by itself grant access to its compartments.
SI.policy_basis: National Security Act of 1947 (as amended) Title I, §105 (b)(1)

TK.short: Talent Keyhole (TK) is an SCI control system designed to protect information and activities related to space-based collection of imagery, signals, measurement and signature intelligence, certain products, processing, and exploitation techniques, and the design, acquisition and operation of reconnaissance satellites.
TK.plain: Talent Keyhole (TK) is one of the main SCI control systems. It protects intelligence from satellites and other space-based collection, along with the systems and techniques behind it.
tips: TK is a control system — a portion names it after the classification: SECRET//TK.
TK compartments (BLUEFISH, IDITAROD, KANDIK — written TK-BLFH and so on) restrict a piece of TK further.

HCS.short: HCS is an SCI control system that comprises two compartments, Operations and Product, and is intended to provide enhanced protection to exceptionally fragile clandestine HUMINT sources, methods, and activities based on assessed value, critical nature, and vulnerability of the information.
HCS.long: HCS is an SCI control system that comprises two compartments, Operations and Product, and is intended to provide enhanced protection to exceptionally fragile clandestine HUMINT sources, methods, and activities based on assessed value, critical nature, and vulnerability of the information. IC clandestine HUMINT collector organizations may elect to use HCS to protect their most sensitive HUMINT information upon the approval of the CIA/Deputy Director for Operations in accordance with national HUMINT policy.
HCS.plain: The HUMINT Control System (HCS) protects the most fragile human-source intelligence — the sources, methods, and activities behind clandestine human collection.
tips: HCS splits into two compartments — Operations (HCS-O) and Product (HCS-P). Mark the one that applies.
A bare HCS is a legacy form; re-mark it as HCS-O and/or HCS-P when you reuse the information in a new product.

SI-G.plain: GAMMA is a compartment within the Special Intelligence (SI) control system. It restricts a piece of SI further, to the people read into GAMMA, and is written SI-G.
tips: A compartment never stands alone — it rides its control system. Write SI-G, not a bare G.
Being read into SI does not grant GAMMA access; GAMMA needs its own read-in.
SI-G.policy_basis: National Security Act of 1947, as amended, Title I, §105 (b)(1)

HCS-O.short: The Operations compartment is used to protect exceptionally fragile and unique IC clandestine HUMINT operations and methods.
HCS-O.plain: Operations is one of the two compartments of the HUMINT Control System (HCS). It protects especially fragile clandestine human-intelligence operations and methods, and is written HCS-O.
tips: HCS splits into two compartments — Operations (HCS-O) and Product (HCS-P). Mark the one that applies; a bare HCS is a legacy form to re-mark.
HCS-O access needs an HCS-O read-in of its own.

HCS-P.short: The Product compartment is used to protect intelligence information (products) intended for dissemination to IC consumers
HCS-P.plain: Product is one of the two compartments of the HUMINT Control System (HCS). It protects finished intelligence products intended for sharing with IC consumers, and is written HCS-P.
tips: HCS splits into two compartments — Product (HCS-P) and Operations (HCS-O). Mark the one that applies; a bare HCS is a legacy form to re-mark.
HCS-P information is marked NOFORN — it is not released to foreign nationals.
Adding a Product sub-compartment (HCS-P followed by a codeword) restricts access further, and raises the lowest level it can carry to TOP SECRET.

TK-BLFH.plain: BLUEFISH is a compartment within the Talent Keyhole (TK) control system, which protects space-based collection. It restricts a piece of TK further, to the people read into BLUEFISH, and is written TK-BLFH.
tips: A compartment never stands alone — it rides its control system. Write TK-BLFH, not a bare BLFH.
Being read into TK does not grant BLUEFISH access; BLUEFISH needs its own read-in.

TK-IDIT.plain: IDITAROD is a compartment within the Talent Keyhole (TK) control system, which protects space-based collection. It restricts a piece of TK further, to the people read into IDITAROD, and is written TK-IDIT.
tips: A compartment never stands alone — it rides its control system. Write TK-IDIT, not a bare IDIT.
Being read into TK does not grant IDITAROD access; IDITAROD needs its own read-in.

TK-KAND.plain: KANDIK is a compartment within the Talent Keyhole (TK) control system, which protects space-based collection. It restricts a piece of TK further, to the people read into KANDIK, and is written TK-KAND.
tips: A compartment never stands alone — it rides its control system. Write TK-KAND, not a bare KAND.
Being read into TK does not grant KANDIK access; KANDIK needs its own read-in.

RD.short: All data concerning (1) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons; (2) the production of special nuclear material; or (3) the use of special nuclear material in the production of energy, but must not include data declassified or removed from the Restricted Data category pursuant to Section 142 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended.
RD.plain: Restricted Data (RD) is nuclear information protected under the Atomic Energy Act — the design, manufacture, or use of atomic weapons, and the production of special nuclear material.
tips: RD is governed by the Atomic Energy Act, not EO 13526, so the Department of Energy sets how it is shared and declassified.
RD is normally marked NOFORN; releasing it to a foreign government requires a specific Atomic Energy Act sharing agreement.
RD.policy_basis: Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended, §141-143

FRD.short: Information removed from the Restricted Data category upon a joint determination by the Departments of Energy and Defense. Such information relates primarily to the military utilization of atomic weapons and can be safeguarded adequately as classified defense information.
FRD.plain: Formerly Restricted Data (FRD) is nuclear information the Departments of Energy and Defense have jointly moved out of the Restricted Data category. It relates mainly to the military use of atomic weapons.
tips: Despite the name, FRD is not declassified — it is still Atomic Energy Act information, not ordinary national-security information.
FRD is normally marked NOFORN; foreign release requires Department of Energy approval.
FRD.policy_basis: Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended, §141-143

TFNI.short: Information concerning the atomic energy programs of other nations that has been removed from the Restricted Data category for use by the Intelligence Community and is safeguarded as NSI under EO 13526.
TFNI.plain: Transclassified Foreign Nuclear Information (TFNI) covers intelligence about other nations' atomic-energy programs that has been moved out of the Restricted Data category and is protected as national-security information.
tips: TFNI is handled as national-security information under EO 13526, not under the Atomic Energy Act rules that govern Restricted Data.

RD-CNWDI.short: TOP SECRET or SECRET Restricted Data (RD) information revealing the theory of operation or design of the components of a fission or thermonuclear bomb, warhead, demolition munitions, or test device.
RD-CNWDI.plain: Critical Nuclear Weapon Design Information (RD-CNWDI) is TOP SECRET or SECRET Restricted Data that reveals how the nuclear components of a weapon are designed or work.
tips: CNWDI only appears on Restricted Data that is already SECRET or TOP SECRET.
It is written as a sub-marking of RD: RD-CNWDI.

DCNI.short: DOD UCNI is unclassified information on security measures for the physical protection of DoD Special Nuclear Material (SNM), equipment or facilities.
DCNI.plain: DoD Unclassified Controlled Nuclear Information (DCNI) is unclassified information about physically protecting the Defense Department's special nuclear material, equipment, or facilities.
tips: DCNI goes only on Unclassified information — it is a handling control, not a classification level.
This is the Defense Department's form; the Department of Energy has its own separate UCNI.
DCNI.policy_basis: Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended

RD-SIGMA.short: A subset of TOP SECRET and SECRET RD information relating to the design, manufacture, or use (including theory, development, storage, characteristics, performance, and effects) of atomic weapons or atomic weapon components.
RD-SIGMA.plain: SIGMA marks a specific category of nuclear-weapon data within Restricted Data, limiting access to the people read into that SIGMA number. It is written RD-SIGMA with one or more numbers, e.g. RD-SIGMA 20.
tips: The SIGMA numbers in use are 14, 15, 18, and 20; list multiple numbers in ascending order with a space between them (RD-SIGMA 18 20).
SIGMA only appears on Restricted Data that is already SECRET or TOP SECRET.
Access needs both a Department of Energy 'Q' clearance and a read-in for each SIGMA number.
RD-SIGMA.policy_basis: Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended, §141-143

FRD-SIGMA.short: A subset of TOP SECRET and SECRET FRD information relating to nuclear weapon data concerning the design, manufacture, or utilization (including theory, development, storage, characteristics, performance, and effects) of atomic weapons or atomic weapon components.
FRD-SIGMA.plain: SIGMA marks a specific category of nuclear-weapon data within Formerly Restricted Data, limiting access to the people read into that SIGMA number. It is written FRD-SIGMA with one or more numbers, e.g. FRD-SIGMA 14.
tips: The SIGMA numbers in use are 14, 15, 18, and 20; list multiple numbers in ascending order with a space between them.
When RD-SIGMA and FRD-SIGMA appear together, the banner lists every SIGMA number under RD-SIGMA — RD takes precedence over FRD.
SIGMA only appears on Formerly Restricted Data that is already SECRET or TOP SECRET.
FRD-SIGMA.policy_basis: Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended, §141-143

NF.short: NOFORN is an explicit foreign release marking used to indicate the information may not be released in any form to foreign governments, foreign nationals, foreign organizations, or non-US citizens without permission of the originator and in accordance with provisions of, ICD 403, NDP-1, and implementation guidance in this document.
NF.plain: Marks information that may not be released in any form to a foreign government, person, or organization — even a close ally — without the originator's permission.
tips: NOFORN and REL TO can't appear on the same portion: NOFORN means no foreign release at all, while REL TO names the countries it can go to.
NF.policy_basis: National Security Act of 1947, as amended, §103 (c)(5)

FOUO.short: Intelligence marking used for UNCLASSIFIED official government information that is withheld from public release until approved for release by the originator.
FOUO.plain: Marks unclassified official government information that is withheld from public release until the originator approves it.
tips: FOUO goes only on Unclassified information — it is a handling caveat, not a classification level.

OC.short: This marking allows originators to maintain knowledge, supervision, and control of the distribution of the ORCON information beyond its original dissemination. Further dissemination of ORCON information requires advance permission from the originator.
OC.plain: Lets the originator keep control of where the information goes. Sharing it any further needs the originator's advance permission.
tips: Any onward sharing of ORCON information needs approval from the originator first.

OC-USGOV.short: The ORCON-USGOV marking is used by IC elements that originate ORCON information to communicate to recipients that the information has been pre-approved for further dissemination without originator approval to the US Government's Executive Branch Departments and Agencies.
OC-USGOV.long: The ORCON-USGOV marking is used by IC elements that originate ORCON information to communicate to recipients that the information has been pre-approved for further dissemination without originator approval to the US Government's Executive Branch Departments and Agencies. It is also approved for use in disseminated analytic products (i.e., not unevaluated or raw intelligence) and other products or information, as determined by the originating agency in consultation with their Office of Legislative Affairs (OLA), provided to congressional Intelligence Committees that have oversight functions and responsibilities.
OC-USGOV.plain: A form of ORCON that is pre-approved for sharing across the US Government's Executive Branch departments and agencies without asking the originator each time.
OC-USGOV.sponsor: DNI National Security Act of 1947, as amended

RELIDO.short: RELIDO is a permissive foreign disclosure and release marking used on information to indicate that the originator has authorized a Senior Foreign Disclosure and Release Authority (SFDRA) to make further sharing decisions for uncaveated intelligence material (intelligence with no restrictive dissemination controls) in accordance with the existing procedures, guidelines, and implementation guidance in this document.
RELIDO.plain: Marks information the originator has cleared for a Senior Foreign Disclosure and Release Authority to make later foreign sharing decisions on.
RELIDO.policy_basis: National Security Act of 1947, as amended, §103 (c)(5)

IMC.short: Controlled Imagery or IMCON is applied to SECRET-level Sensitive Analytical Techniques (SATs) that have been approved by the Sensitive Analytical Techniques Panel (SATP).
IMC.plain: Protects sensitive imagery analytic techniques that the Sensitive Analytical Techniques Panel has approved.

RS.short: This term is used to protect especially sensitive imaging capabilities and exploitation techniques.
RS.plain: Protects especially sensitive imaging capabilities and the techniques used to exploit them.

DSEN.short: Unclassified information originated by DEA that requires protection against unauthorized disclosure to protect sources and methods of investigative activity, evidence, and the integrity of pretrial investigative reports.
DSEN.plain: Marks unclassified DEA information that needs protection to safeguard investigative sources, methods, evidence, and pretrial reports.

PROPIN.short: Marking to identify information provided by a commercial firm or private source under an express or implied understanding that the information will be protected as a proprietary trade secret or proprietary data believed to have actual or potential value.
PROPIN.plain: Identifies information a company or private source provided on the understanding that it will be protected as a trade secret or proprietary data.

FISA.short: The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) of 1978, as amended, prescribes procedures for the physical and electronic surveillance and collection of "foreign intelligence information" between or among "foreign powers" on territory under United States control.
FISA.plain: Marks information handled under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, which sets the procedures for surveillance and collection of foreign intelligence.

ND.short: This control is used only on messages of the highest sensitivity between the President, the Secretary of State, and Chief of Mission. No further dissemination is allowed to any other than the original addressee(s) without the approval of the Executive Secretary.

XD.short: Information with exclusive distribution to officers with essential need-to-know. This caption is used only for highly sensitive traffic between the White House, the Secretary, Deputy, or Under Secretaries of State and Chiefs of Missions.

LES.short: LAW ENFORCEMENT SENSITIVE (LES) information is **unclassified** information originated by agencies or elements with law enforcement missions that may be used in criminal prosecution and that requires protection against unauthorized disclosure to protect sources and methods, investigative activity, evidence, or the integrity of pretrial investigative reports.

SBU.short: Administrative unclassified information originated from within the Department of State, which warrants a degree of protection and administrative control and meets criteria for exemption from mandatory public disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act.

DS.short: Marking used to identify unclassified maps and geospatial products and data sets, which the Secretary of Defense may withhold from public release.

SSI.short: As defined in 49 C.F.R. 15.5 and 1520.5, information (unclassified) obtained or developed in the conduct of security activities, including research and development, the disclosure of which Department of Homeland Security (DHS)/Transportation Security Administration (TSA) or Department of Transportation (DOT) has determined would (1) constitute an unwarranted invasion of privacy (including, but not limited to, information contained in any personnel, medical, or similar file); (2) reveal trade secrets or privileged or confidential information obtained from any person; or (3) be detrimental to the safety or security of transportation.
